plan.title: bug(scope): scope:complete leaves the completing brief's own plan.items[].status pending and xBRIEFInfo.updated stale

narratives.Description: scope:complete moves a brief to completed/ and sets plan.status to completed, but leaves plan.items[].status on pending and never refreshes xBRIEFInfo.updated. Mirror registry sync already reconciles PROJECT-DEFINITION and specification items; the completing brief itself is the gap. Fix terminal transitions in runTransition to advance non-terminal own items and refresh the envelope updated stamp.
narratives.Overview:
Filed as a **consumer of the framework**, not a maintainer — apologies if any of this is already understood internally. Everything below was verified against the installed package on one project; I have not read the framework source repo.

## Summary

`deft scope:complete` moves a scope brief to `xbrief/completed/` and sets `plan.status = "completed"`, but leaves the brief's **own** `plan.items[].status` on `pending` and never refreshes the document-level `xBRIEFInfo.updated`. The result is a completed brief that internally still reads as unstarted work.

This is the same reconcile obligation you already closed twice for the *mirror* artifacts — #1527 for `PROJECT-DEFINITION` and #2566 / #2592 for `specification.xbrief.json`. Both of those flip `plan.items[].status` on a terminal transition. The one artifact left unreconciled is the completing brief itself, which is the authoritative record rather than a projection.

Our operators have hand-corrected this on three consecutive completion PRs and a bot flagged it on a fourth, which is why I'm filing rather than continuing to patch it locally.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| CLI | `@deftai/directive@0.85.0` (engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.85.0`), global npm install |
| Vendored content | `.deft/core` at `v0.84.0` (`managed_by: npm`, deposited 2026-07-23) |
| `xbrief/.deft-version` | `0.84.0` |
| Layout | `xbrief/` (v0.8), consumer install (not a framework source checkout) |
| OS / shell | macOS (darwin 25.5.0), zsh |

## Observed behavior

1. A brief in `xbrief/active/` has `plan.status: "running"` and `plan.items[*].status: "pending"`.
2. The work ships and the PR merges.
3. Operator runs `deft scope:complete -- xbrief/active/<brief>.xbrief.json`.
4. The file moves to `xbrief/completed/` with `plan.status: "completed"`, `plan.updated` refreshed, and `plan.metadata.completedAt` stamped.
5. **`plan.items[*].status` is still `"pending"`** on every item, including items that fully shipped.
6. **`xBRIEFInfo.updated`** still holds the timestamp from before the completion.

## Expected behavior

On a terminal transition, either:

- set the brief's own `plan.items[*].status` to the terminal status (with whatever cascade rule you prefer for `subItems`) and refresh `xBRIEFInfo.updated` alongside `plan.updated`; **or**
- document that `plan.items[].status` on a completed brief is not authoritative, and stop having deterministic reviewers flag it (see the SLizard rule below, which currently treats it as a logic error).

Either resolution is fine from a consumer's perspective. The current state is the one that costs time: the field looks authoritative, a bot says it's wrong, and the tooling won't fix it.

## Reproduction

```bash
deft scope:activate -- xbrief/proposed/<brief>.xbrief.json   # -> active/, status running, items pending
# ... ship the work ...
deft scope:complete -- xbrief/active/<brief>.xbrief.json     # -> completed/, status completed
jq '.plan.status, [.plan.items[].status], .xBRIEFInfo.updated' xbrief/completed/<brief>.xbrief.json
# "completed"
# ["pending","pending","pending","pending"]
# "<pre-completion timestamp>"
```

## Evidence from the installed code

`@deftai/directive-core@0.85.0`, `dist/scope/transition.js` (built from `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts`), the mutation block of `runTransition`:

```js
const nowIso = utcNowIso(now);
planObj.status = targetStatus;
planObj.updated = nowIso;
if (act === "complete") {
    stampCompletionMetadata(planObj, projectRoot, nowIso);
}
```

That is the complete set of in-document mutations. `stampCompletionMetadata` (`dist/scope/capacity-stamp.js`) only writes `plan.metadata.completedAt` and `plan.metadata.capacityBucket`. Nothing in the function reads or writes `planObj.items`, and nothing touches the top-level `xBRIEFInfo` / `vBRIEFInfo` envelope — `planObj.updated` is `plan.updated`, a different field.

**The asymmetry is visible in the same function.** A few lines later `runTransition` calls:

```js
syncProjectDefinitionAfterScopeMove(data, resolvedPath, destPath, vbriefRoot, targetStatus);
syncSpecificationAfterScopeMove(data, resolvedPath, destPath, vbriefRoot, targetStatus);
```

Both route into `dist/scope/registry-artifact-sync.js`, which does exactly the thing the brief itself doesn't get:

```js
if (i.status !== targetStatus) {
    i.status = targetStatus;
}
```

So on a completion the framework reaches out and reconciles item status in two derived registries while leaving the source artifact stale. From the outside that reads like an oversight rather than a decision, but I may be missing the rationale.

## Occurrences in one consumer repo (deftai/BestiMax)

Three PRs whose entire diff is the hand-correction, plus a bot finding:

| PR | Brief | Manual fix-up in the diff |
|---|---|---|
| [#119](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/pull/119) | `2026-07-22-land-dependabot-patch-minor` | `items[].status: pending -> completed`, `xBRIEFInfo.updated` bumped |
| [#121](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/pull/121) | `2026-07-22-land-eslint-10` | same two corrections |
| [#138](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/pull/138) | `2026-07-26-rls-boundary-hardening` | same two corrections, on four items |

PR #138's commit message names the gap directly:

> `deft scope:complete` flips plan.status and stamps metadata.completedAt but leaves item statuses and xBRIEFInfo.updated behind, so those are corrected here.

**A deterministic reviewer already treats this as a defect.** SLizard's review on [BestiMax PR #127](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/pull/127) raised rule `directive-2584-recall`:

> **directive-2584-recall**: [Logic Error] Active xBRIEF plan.status is still "running"/"active" and all plan.items are pending/proposed even though this PR implements the work.

Worth being precise about what that finding proves, since it is adjacent rather than identical: it fired on the *implementation* PR, where the brief was still active, so it is about the implementing agent not updating item statuses. Combined with this report the picture is that **no surface in the toolchain ever transitions a brief's own `items[].status`** — not the implementer, not the lifecycle command. An operator following the documented flow exactly still ends up with a stale corpus and a bot finding.

Three repetitions of an identical manual correction, plus an automated reviewer flagging the same field, is what pushed this from "our habit is wrong" to "the tooling has a gap".

## Impact

Low severity, steady cost. Nothing breaks and no gate fails — `deft check` and `vbrief:validate` both pass on a brief with completed status and pending items, because the fields are schema-independent.

What it costs:

- **Every completion needs a hand-edit**, or the corpus accumulates briefs that are internally contradictory.
- **Reviewers flag it**, so each completion PR carries a finding the operator must dismiss or fix.
- **Item-level status becomes unusable as a data source** — you can't answer "which planned items actually shipped" across the corpus, because the answer is "all of them say pending".
- **It is invisible in the moment.** `scope:complete` exits 0 with a success message; the staleness is only found later, by a reviewer or a reader.

## Prior art in this repo

- **#1527** (closed) — *"scope:complete updates PROJECT-DEFINITION references but leaves registry item status stale."* Same defect, mirror artifact, fixed.
- **#2566 / #2592** (closed) — *"scope:complete moves scopes to completed/ but leaves specification.xbrief.json roadmap item statuses stale."* Same defect, second mirror artifact, fixed. #2566's framing applies verbatim here: *"Lifecycle folder moves succeed; the item statuses are never reconciled."*
- **#1674** (open) — *"task scope:cancel doesn't stamp cancellation metadata (cancelledAt / cancellationReason / item status / Disposition)."* This is the closest existing issue and it already names the exact gap, including the asymmetry:

  > `plan.items[*].status` — left as `proposed` (etc.) instead of `cancelled` when the parent is cancelled. (The existing PROJECT-DEFINITION sync updates *that* plan's items, but not the scope vBRIEF's own `plan.items[]`.)

  But #1674 is scoped to `cancel`; its proposed-fix item 4 asks whether the same symmetry should extend to `fail`, and does not mention `complete`. **If you'd rather widen #1674 to cover all terminal transitions than carry a second issue, that seems cleaner and I'm happy for this one to be closed as folded in.** I filed separately because `complete` is by far the highest-traffic verb and #1674 has sat at P3 since June with no comments.
- **#1618** (open RFC) — *"Separate source-of-truth from materialized views — demote plan.items."* If `plan.items` is heading for demotion, that changes the right fix here (documenting non-authority rather than reconciling), which is the other reason I'd rather surface this than keep patching locally.

## Suggested fix

Mirroring the shape of #1527 / #2592, inside `runTransition`:

1. On terminal transitions (`complete`, and by symmetry `fail` / `cancel` per #1674), set the brief's own `plan.items[*].status` to the terminal status, recursing into `subItems`.
2. Decide and document the cascade rule for items that legitimately did **not** ship. A blanket flip to `completed` would overwrite a deliberate `cancelled` or `deferred` item. The conservative rule — only advance items still in a non-terminal state (`pending` / `proposed` / `running`), leave already-terminal items alone — preserves operator intent and is what our hand-edits have been doing by eye.
3. Refresh `xBRIEFInfo.updated` (v0.8) / `vBRIEFInfo.updated` (v0.6) in the same write as `plan.updated`, matching whichever envelope the document actually carries. #2346 / #2363 is the cautionary precedent here: a writer that stamped `vBRIEFInfo` unconditionally corrupted v0.8 files and blocked a release.
4. If instead the intended contract is that a completed brief's item statuses are *not* authoritative, document that and retire the `directive-2584-recall` reviewer rule — the two currently contradict each other.

## Two adjacent observations, recorded for context only

Neither is part of this report; happy to file either separately if useful.

**(a) `plan.completedNote` is rejected by the conformance gate, and the canonical replacement isn't obvious from the error.** The two briefs completed by the PRs in the table above (BestiMax #119 and #121) use bare `plan.completedNote`, which the #1620 gate now flags: *"detected 4 bare key(s) ... Every vBRIEF key MUST be spec-core, x-directive/-namespaced, legacy-vbrief-namespaced, or x-xbrief/-namespaced."* Reading `dist/policy/plan-extensions.js` makes clear this is **intended** tightening under #1650, and that the canonical target is `x-directive/completedNote` with `dist/category-b-namespace/index.js` as the codemod. So: not a bug, and I'm not filing it. The friction is only that the gate's remediation text lists three namespace prefixes generically without naming `x-directive/completedNote` as *the* answer for this specific key — our operator guessed `plan.metadata.completedNote`, which is conformant but off-canon. A one-line hint in the message would have prevented that.

**(b) The conformance gate appears not to run on consumer installs.** On a consumer project, `deft verify:vbrief-conformance` with no arguments prints `OK: vBRIEF validation passed` and exits 0, while `deft verify:vbrief-conformance --all` on the identical tree exits non-zero with 4 findings. Looking at `dist/vbrief-validate/main.js`, `cmdVbriefValidate` only routes to `runConformance` when `argv[0] === "conformance"`, or when `--staged` / `--all` is present — a bare invocation falls through to the schema validator (its `--help` even prints `usage: vbrief_validate.py ...`). Separately, `dist/check/gate-lists.js` lists `verify:vbrief-conformance` in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` but not in `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`. Net effect on our install: the only path that actually runs the #1620 scan is the pre-commit hook's `--staged` mode, which sees newly staged files only — so four pre-existing violations have sat in the tree unreported. This may well be deliberate scoping; flagging in case the bare-verb fallthrough is not.

## Also from this install

The same project filed #2826 on 2026-07-24 (empty open-issue inventory treated as stale, blocking write hooks) — since closed by #2830, thank you. Noting it so you can see these come from the same consumer install and framework line, in case that's useful for correlating reports.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer completing a scope brief, I want scope:complete to reconcile the brief's own plan.items status and xBRIEFInfo.updated, so that completed briefs do not look unstarted and reviewers stop flagging false positives.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: In packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts runTransition mutation block: on terminal transitions (complete, and by symmetry fail/cancel), advance the brief's own plan.items[*].status (and subItems) only when still non-terminal (pending/proposed/running), leave already-terminal items alone. Refresh xBRIEFInfo.updated (v0.8) or vBRIEFInfo.updated (v0.6) in the same write as plan.updated. Add unit tests covering complete with mixed item statuses and envelope stamp. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] cites #2862. Do not expand #1674 cancel-only unless the same helper is shared cleanly.
